issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:400-401`, `sort_value()` implements artist sorting as `return (row["artist"].lower(), row["year"] or 9999)`. Because `0` is falsy in Python, artworks dated to astronomical year `0` (1 BC) are coerced to `9999` and sorted after modern works instead of before year 1.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`
- `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: converting years to string representations or special casing 0 without distinguishing `None` from integer `0` is a failure of this issue.
- Do not modify playlist filtering or random shuffle logic.

## Tasks
- [ ] Update `sort_value()` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py` to use `row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999` for artist sort.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` asserting works dated year `0` sort before positive years when sorting playlists by artist.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` passes with 100% success.
- Sorting playlist rows containing works dated year `0` and year `1500` by artist places the year `0` work before the year `1500` work.
- Deliberate break: revert `row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999` to `row["year"] or 9999` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`, run `pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`, and verify that the year 0 sort test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Use explicit `None` checking (`row["year"] if row["year"] is not None else 9999`) in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`.
issues.title: fix(playlist): prevent year 0 falsiness in playlist artist sort

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:1397-1411` and `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:1413-1417`, `_write_sidecar_atomic()` and `_append_subject_tag_event()` open file handles with `os.fdopen(fd, "w")` and `open(SUBJECT_TAG_EVENTS, "a")` without specifying `encoding="utf-8"`. On environments where the default locale encoding is ASCII or non-UTF-8, serializing sidecars containing non-ASCII artist names or titles raises `UnicodeEncodeError`.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`
- `tests/test_eink_feed_endpoints.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: setting `ensure_ascii=True` in `json.dumps()` to escape non-ASCII characters without specifying UTF-8 encoding on file handles is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter the atomic tempfile rename and chmod logic.

## Tasks
- [ ] Specify `encoding="utf-8"` in `os.fdopen()` and `open()` within `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` for `_write_sidecar_atomic` and `_append_subject_tag_event`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_eink_feed_endpoints.py` asserting `_write_sidecar_atomic` successfully writes non-ASCII UTF-8 characters under non-UTF-8 default locale settings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_eink_feed_endpoints.py` passes with 100% success.
- Writing a sidecar containing non-ASCII artist names such as `Albrecht Dürer` via `_write_sidecar_atomic()` produces valid UTF-8 encoded files without raising UnicodeEncodeError.
- Deliberate break: remove `encoding="utf-8"` from `os.fdopen` in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`, run `pytest tests/test_eink_feed_endpoints.py`, and verify the non-ASCII write test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Pass `encoding="utf-8"` to both `os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8")` and `open(SUBJECT_TAG_EVENTS, "a", encoding="utf-8")` in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`.
issues.title: fix(api): specify explicit utf-8 encoding in atomic sidecar writes

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py:422-434`, `acuity_blur_radius()` validates inputs with `if ppi <= 0 or viewing_distance_cm <= 0: raise ValueError(...)`. When `ppi` or `viewing_distance_cm` is `float('nan')`, `nan <= 0` evaluates to `False`, bypassing the guard and returning `nan` silently instead of raising `ValueError`.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py`
- `tests/test_dither_metric_discriminates.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching NaN return values downstream in Gaussian blur calculations without validating input parameters in `acuity_blur_radius` is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter the `ARCMINUTES_PER_RADIAN` optical constant.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add finite number validation to `acuity_blur_radius()` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py` checking `math.isfinite(ppi)` and `math.isfinite(viewing_distance_cm)`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_dither_metric_discriminates.py` asserting `acuity_blur_radius` raises `ValueError` on NaN and infinite inputs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_dither_metric_discriminates.py` passes with 100% success.
- Calling `acuity_blur_radius(float("nan"), 50.0)` or `acuity_blur_radius(150.0, float("inf"))` raises `ValueError`.
- Deliberate break: remove `math.isfinite` check in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py`, run `pytest tests/test_dither_metric_discriminates.py`, and verify that the NaN parameter test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Check `not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or isinstance(v, bool) or not math.isfinite(v) or v <= 0` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py`.
issues.title: fix(eink): guard non-finite inputs in acuity_blur_radius

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py:88-120`, `dim_compat()` compares dimensions against `tolerance` with `difference <= tolerance`. When `tolerance` is `float('nan')` or negative, `difference <= tolerance` evaluates to `False` even for identical dimensions (`dim_compat("50 x 50 cm", "50 x 50 cm", tolerance=float("nan"))` returns `('mismatch', 0.0)` instead of rejecting invalid tolerance).

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py`
- `tests/test_dimension_utils.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: wrapping float comparisons in try-except blocks without validating that tolerance is a finite non-negative number is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter dimension parsing regular expressions or unit conversion factors.

## Tasks
- [ ] Validate `tolerance` in `dim_compat()` within `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py` raising `ValueError` when `tolerance` is non-finite, not a float/int, or strictly negative.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_dimension_utils.py` asserting `dim_compat` raises `ValueError` on NaN, infinite, or negative tolerance values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_dimension_utils.py` passes with 100% success.
- Calling `dim_compat("50 x 50 cm", "50 x 50 cm", tolerance=float("nan"))` or `tolerance=-0.1` raises `ValueError`.
- Deliberate break: remove tolerance validation from `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py`, run `pytest tests/test_dimension_utils.py`, and verify tolerance validation tests fail; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Validate `isinstance(tolerance, (int, float)) and not isinstance(tolerance, bool) and math.isfinite(tolerance) and tolerance >= 0.0` in `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py`.
issues.title: fix(parsers): validate finite non-negative tolerance in dim_compat

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py:427-431`, `inherit()` fills empty metadata fields from the parent sidecar using direct reference assignment `meta[field] = parent_value`. When parent fields contain mutable containers such as dictionaries or lists (for example `artist`, `holder`, `site`, or `rights`), in-place modifications to the child sidecar mutate the parent sidecar object in memory.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`
- `tests/test_variants.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: shallow copying dictionary references without deep copying nested mutable data structures is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter the list of inheritable fields or stable identifier merge rules.

## Tasks
- [ ] Deep copy inherited metadata values in `inherit()` within `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py` using `copy.deepcopy(parent_value)`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_variants.py` asserting mutating child metadata fields does not alter parent sidecar dictionaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_variants.py` passes with 100% success.
- Creating a child variant with `inherit(parent_meta, child_meta)` and mutating `child_meta["artist"]["name"]` leaves `parent_meta["artist"]["name"]` unchanged.
- Deliberate break: change `copy.deepcopy(parent_value)` back to `parent_value` in `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`, run `pytest tests/test_variants.py`, and verify that the mutation independence test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Import `copy` and use `copy.deepcopy` when assigning inheritable fields in `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`.
issues.title: fix(identity): deepcopy mutable metadata values during variant inheritance

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py:124-173`, `build()` collects scored works with `[(features_of(sc), s) for sc, s in rated if s is not None]`. When a score `s` is `float('nan')` or non-numeric, `s > split` and `s < split` comparisons evaluate to False, treating all ratings as ties at median `NaN`. This produces an empty `PreferenceVector` with `split_value=nan` despite valid scores being present in the input.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py`
- `tests/test_rocchio_preference.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `TypeError` during centroid math without filtering non-finite scores during initial rated filtering is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter Rocchio `BETA` or `GAMMA` centroid weighting constants.

## Tasks
- [ ] Filter non-finite and boolean ratings in `build()` within `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py` using `isinstance(s, (int, float)) and not isinstance(s, bool) and math.isfinite(s)`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_rocchio_preference.py` asserting `build()` ignores NaN ratings and correctly builds preference vectors from remaining valid scores.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_rocchio_preference.py` passes with 100% success.
- Supplying `[(work_a, float("nan")), (work_b, 9.0), (work_c, 3.0)]` to `build()` calculates a valid median split and non-empty preference weights without NaN corruption.
- Deliberate break: remove `math.isfinite` check for rated scores in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py`, run `pytest tests/test_rocchio_preference.py`, and verify that the NaN rating test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Ensure `split` is computed only over finite scores in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py`.
issues.title: fix(preference): filter non-finite ratings in rocchio build

issues.body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py:236-274`, `apply_saturation_cap()` computes allowed candidate counts per bucket using `int(round(batch_cap * float(share) * tolerance))`. If an archive share is `float('nan')` or `float('inf')`, or if `tolerance` is non-finite, Python raises `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer` or `OverflowError`. Furthermore, when `batch_cap <= 0`, `allowed[bucket] = max(1, ...)` forces each bucket to allow at least 1 candidate, causing non-empty selections when zero items were requested.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`
- `tests/test_selection_lenses.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `ValueError` at call sites or returning unvalidated pools without sanitizing `batch_cap`, shares, and tolerance is a failure of this issue.
- Do not modify candidate ranking order or round-robin selection logic outside saturation capping.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add entry guard for `batch_cap <= 0` returning `([], SaturationReport(...))` and validate `0.0 <= float(share) <= 1.0` and `float(tolerance) >= 0.0` with `math.isfinite` in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_selection_lenses.py` asserting `apply_saturation_cap` handles `batch_cap <= 0`, NaN/inf shares, and non-finite tolerances without raising exceptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_selection_lenses.py` passes with 100% success.
- Calling `apply_saturation_cap(pool, batch_cap=0, archive_shares={"landscape": 0.5}, bucket_of=lambda x: x["bucket"])` returns an empty candidate list and empty headroom.
- Calling `apply_saturation_cap(pool, batch_cap=10, archive_shares={"landscape": float("nan")}, bucket_of=lambda x: x["bucket"], tolerance=float("nan"))` executes without raising ValueError or OverflowError.
- Deliberate break: remove finite share validation in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`, run `pytest tests/test_selection_lenses.py`, and verify that the non-finite share tests fail; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Use `math.isfinite` to sanitize `share` and `tolerance` before computing bucket limits in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`.
issues.title: fix(selection): guard non-finite inputs and zero batch cap in apply_saturation_cap

issues.body:
> **Not dispatchable to an agent — needs physical hardware that does not exist yet.** Tracking only; do not add `agents:auto-pilot`.

## Why

Epic #23 is closed because its blocker (which panel, push vs SD) is resolved and **both** transports are built, tested and merged. But #23's goal says deliver to the *physical* panels, and no panel has been bought. Everything is verified against the app, nothing against glass.

Two specific things are unknown until a real device exists, and both are recorded here so they are not rediscovered:

**1. The palette is estimated, not measured.** `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py` ships Spectra 6 primaries that are reasonable guesses. Every palette carries `measured: False`, and every exported SD card states so in `playlist.json` and `README.txt`. No vendor at these sizes publishes a colour profile, gamut volume or Delta-E — `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` calls this the survey's central open gap. Replacing six RGB triples upgrades every card and feed retroactively.

**2. Colour may not be good enough at all.** The one independent hands-on report of a 28.5" colour unit describes photographs as "dark, desaturated, and low resolution", with no pure white — only "a yellowish grey" — and **monochrome reproductions faring markedly better than colour**. The survey's own recommendation is to measure a unit before committing the pipeline to colour e-paper. If mono wins, the `gray16` target already exists.

## Scope

First-light verification of the existing pipeline against one purchased panel. No new features.

## Non-Goals

- No new render targets, transports or UI. Both transports are done.
- Not buying the hardware — that is the owner's decision, and the survey's US-availability read is in `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md`.
- Not a colour-management system. Six measured primaries is the deliverable, not an ICC workflow.

## Tasks

- [ ] Photograph a rendered card under controlled light and sample the six Spectra 6 primaries from a full-coverage test pattern; record the measured RGB.
- [ ] Replace the estimated tuples in `palette.py` `SPECTRA6` with the measured values and set `measured=True`.
- [ ] Re-run `dither_error` on a reference work with measured vs estimated palettes and record the change in `perceived_rgb_distance`.
- [ ] Exercise the chosen transport end to end on the device: for SD, write a card with `scripts/make_eink_card.py --write` and confirm the panel plays it in filename order; for network, point the device at `/feed/{id}/current` and confirm it advances across a rotation interval.
- [ ] Compare a colour render against a `gray16` render of the same work on the panel and record which reads better, per the survey's warning.
- [ ] Update `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` to replace "no vendor publishes a colour profile" with the measured result for the device bought.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` still passes with the measured palette in place (the palette-invariant tests must hold for real values, not just estimates).
- [ ] `get_palette("spectra6").measured is True`, and a freshly exported card's `playlist.json` shows `"palette_measured": true` with no `palette_warning`.
- [ ] A photograph of the panel showing an exported work is attached to this issue — the observable gate, since no automated check can see glass.
- [ ] The panel is confirmed to advance through at least two works via the chosen transport, evidenced by two photographs or a device log.
- [ ] A one-line verdict is recorded in the survey: colour usable / mono preferred, with the measured perceived-error figures behind it.
